title: DOD Halts Use of Anthropic AI After Court Upholds Supply Chain Risk Designation
key_facts: A Pentagon spokesperson told MeriTalk the department has ceased the use of Anthropic products; the Defense Department is now styled the Department of War.
The halt comes eight months after Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth designated Anthropic a supply chain risk.
The dispute began when the Pentagon wanted Claude used for 'all lawful uses' and Anthropic objected to mass surveillance and fully autonomous weapons.
On 25 Sep 2026 the D.C. Circuit upheld the designation 2-1, letting the department keep excluding Anthropic's models from its systems and defence contract work.
On 27 Aug 2026 US District Judge Rita Lin in California sided with Anthropic against broader federal restrictions from the same dispute.
Anthropic could ask the full D.C. Circuit to reconsider or ask the Supreme Court to take the case.
quote_evidence: "The Department of War has ceased the use of Anthropic products," a department spokesperson told MeriTalk.
The company prevailed in its California case challenging the administration's broader restrictions but lost its challenge to the Pentagon's supply chain risk designation in Washington.
why_it_matters_hint: The Pentagon is on record as no longer using Anthropic's AI, and the two court rulings leave Anthropic with a mixed result and possible further appeals.
event_date: Halt reported 5 Oct 2026 (BBC, our 6 Oct edition); D.C. Circuit ruling 25 Sep 2026
notes: Homeland Security Today page was blocked (403); MeriTalk carries the same story and was read in full. Yesterday's BBC account said Claude was still used last week for intelligence work.
